alternatives.argument: The carrier gives the complete finite-label nonnegative score-loss definition, including Borel measurability, the zero-times-infinity convention, expected loss, propriety, strict propriety, and the logarithmic and Brier losses. It is a definition; no imported theorem is used as a substitute for the definition.

The carrier proves the finite-sum log-loss regret identity as KL divergence, proves nonnegativity and the equality case by the logarithm integral inequality including zero coordinates, and proves the Brier regret identity as squared Euclidean distance. These local calculations establish strict propriety independently of the cited treatment.

The carrier obtains a measurable posterior from the stated standard-Borel disintegration suppliers, applies the locally defined pointwise proper-score inequality at each feature value, and integrates it through the Bayes-risk supplier. Its uniqueness argument uses finite posterior risk, nonnegative integral zero, and strict propriety. The full argument is written in the carrier.

The carrier specifies a finite independent feature-label law, checks that every feature-conditional label vector equals the constant forecast, then verifies the forecast-event integral identities directly for every Borel subset of the finite simplex.
